hints.content:
We define function $g$ using a definite integral of function $h$. For every $x$-value, we calculate $g(x)$ by taking the definite integral of $h$ from $-4$ to $x$.

So to calculate $g(\goldD{-1})$ we need to take the definite integral of $h$ from $-4$ to $\goldD{-1}$:

$g(\goldD{-1})=\displaystyle\int_{-4}^{\goldD{-1}}h(t)\,dt$

This represents the net area between the graph of $h(t)$ and the $x$-axis from $x=-4$ to $x=-1$.

We can find $\displaystyle\int_{-4}^{\goldD{-1}}h(t)\,dt$ using geometric area formulas.

![The graph of function h has the region between the segments and the x-axis, between x = negative 4 and x = negative 1, shaded. The segment at the top of the shaded region starts at (negative 4, 8), moves rightward to (negative 3, 8), moves downward and ends at (negative 1, 6).](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/3c1369d11df131f076a6864d64e55ff2a10fd29c)

We have a $3$ by $8$ rectangle less a $2$ by $2$ right triangle, so in total the area is $22$.
